div.ab: XXXVIII[I]. Eallum frioum monnum ðas dagas sien forgifene, butan þeowum monnum ⁊ esnewyrhtan: XII dagas on gehhol ⁊ ðone dæg þe Crist ðone deofol oferswiðde ⁊ scs. XXXVIIII. Eallum freomonnum ðas dagas syn forgifene, buton ðeowum monnum ⁊ esnewyrhtum: XII dagas on gehhol ⁊ ðone dæg ðe Crist oferswiðde ðone deofol ⁊ scs. Gregorius gemynddæg ⁊ seofon dagas to eastrum ond VII ofer and an dæg to sc̄e Petres tide ⁊ sc̄e Paules ⁊ on hærfest ða fullan wucan ær sc̄a Marian mæssan ⁊ æt Ealra haligra weorþunge ænne dæg; ⁊ IIII Wodnesdagas on IIII ymbrenwucan ðeowum monnum eallum syn forgifen, ðam ðe him leofost sy to syllanne æghwæt ðæs þe him ænig mon for Godes nomon gesylle oððe heo on ænigum heora hwilstyccum geearnian magen.

Omnibus liberis hominibus dies isti condonati sunt preter seruis et pauperibus operariis: XII dies in sancto natali Domini et dies in qua dominus Jesus de diabolo triumphauit et sancti Gregorii memorialis dies et septem dies in pascha et septem supra et unus dies in festo beatorum apostolorum Petri et Pauli et in Augusto plena ebdomada ante festum beate Marie et in omnium sanctorum ueneratione I dies; et quatuor dies Mercurii in quatuor legitimis ieiuniis seruis omnibus indulti sunt dare cui magis uoluerint, uel qui eis pro Dei nomine aliquid benefecerit uel ipsi deseruire poterint in aliqua portione uicis sue.

{XXXVIII[I]} Eallum frioum monnum ðas dagas sien forgifene, butan þeowum monnum ⁊ esnewyrhtan: XII dagas on gehhol ⁊ ðone dæg þe Crist ðone deofol oferswiðde 7 sanctus Gregorius gemynddæg ⁊ VII dagas to eastron ⁊ VII ofer ⁊ an dæg æt sancte Petres tide ⁊ sancte Paulus ⁊ on hærfeste ða fullan wican ǽr sancta Marian mæssan ⁊ æt eallra haligra weorðunge anne dæg; ⁊ IIII Wodnesdagas on IIII ymbrenwicum ðeowum monnum eallum sien forgifen, þam þe him leofost sie to sellanne æghwæt ðæs ðe him ænig mon for Godes noman geselle oððe hie on ænegum hiora hwilsticcum geearnian mægen.

Allen freien Leuten seien folgende Tage freigegeben (jedoch nicht unfreien Leuten und Lohnarbeitern): 12 Tage zu Weihnachten und der Tag, da Christus den Teufel überwand, und des heil. Gregor Gedächtnisstag und 7 Tage zu Ostern und 7 nachher und ein Tag zu des heil. Petrus und des heil. Paulus Fest und im Herbst die volle Woche vor der heil. Maria Messe und zu Aller Heiligen Ehre ein Tag; und 4 Mittwochen in den 4 Quatemberwochen seien allen unfreien Leuten freigegeben, um dem, der ihnen der liebste ist, etwas davón hinzugeben, was [entweder] ihnen irgend jemand in Gottes Namen schenkt oder sie [selbst] in einigen [freien] Augenblicken verdienen können.

To all free people let the following days be granted as holidays (but not to unfree people and hired labourers): 12 days at Christmas, and the day on which Christ overcame the devil, and St Gregory’s commemoration day, and 7 days at Easter and 7 after, and one day at the feast of St Peter and St Paul, and in autumn the full week before the mass of St Mary, and one day in honour of All Saints; and let 4 Wednesdays in the 4 Ember weeks be granted to all unfree people, so that they may give to whomever is dearest to them anything of what [either] anyone gives them in God’s name or they [themselves] can earn in any [free] moments.

The following days shall be granted [as holidays] to all free men, though not to slaves and hired labourers: twelve days at Christmas and the day on which Christ overcame the devil; the anniversary of St Gregory; seven days before Easter and seven days after; one day at the festival of St Peter and St Paul; and in autumn, the full week before St Mary’s mass; and one day at the celebration of All Saints. The four Wednesdays in the four Ember weeks shall be granted [as holidays] to all slaves whose chief desire is to sell anything which has been given to them in God's name, or which they are able to acquire by their labour in any portions of time at their disposal.

These days are to be given to all free men, but not to slaves or unfree labourers: 12 days at Christmas, and the day on which Christ overcame the devil, and the anniversary of St Gregory, and seven days at Easter and seven days after, and one day at the feast of St Peter and St Paul, and in harvesttime the whole week before the feast of St Mary, and one day at the feast of All Saints. And the four Wednesdays in the four Ember weeks are to be given to all slaves, to sell to whomsoever they choose anything of what anyone has given them in God’s name, or of what they can earn in any of their leisure moments.

To all free men these days are given [off from work] except for slaves and esnas: twelve days at Christmas, and the day that Christ overcame the devil, and the commemoration day of St Gregory, and seven days before Easter and seven after, and one day at the feastday of St. Peter and St. Paul, and in the harvest the full week before St. Mary’s mass, and at the honoring of All Saints one day. And four Wednesdays on the four weeks in which Ember days fall shall be given to all slaves, so that they can give to whoever is most dear to them a portion of whatever any man gives them in God’s name or that they may earn in their fragments of time [in which they work on their own].

Erstens Hintersassen im Herrschaftsgut, Bauern und Kötter, die Fron (s. d. Gl 12) leisten, und zweitens Landarbeiter ohne Grundbesitz, die im Gutshofe, auch des Bauern, wohnen. Ihr Ggs. sind Unfreie (s. d. Gl 1e), zu denen auch die esnewyrhtan gehören müssen; ich würde jetzt lieber ‘knechtischen Arbeitern’ dafür setzen

Firstly, tenants on the lord’s estate, peasants and cottars who perform labour services (see that word in Gl 12), and secondly, landless farm labourers who live on the farmstead, including that of the peasant. In contrast to them are the unfree (see that word in Gl 1e), to whom the esnewyrhtan must also belong; I would now rather put ‘servile labourers’ for them
H cor. modernisiert. — Den ceorlas zu ‘Hisseburn’ gibt je eine Woche frei zu Weihnachten, Ostern, Rogationes Urk. a. 901 Bi 594
H cor. modernizes. — A charter of a. 901, Bi 594, grants the ceorlas at ‘Hisseburn’ a week free each at Christmas, Easter and Rogations
Anakoluth; Akkusativ steht hier und weiterhin, als begänne das Gesetz: ‘wir haben freigegeben’
Anacoluthon; the accusative is used here and further on, as if the law began: ‘we have granted free’

15. Aug.; vgl. Gl Maria 4; Mariä Geburt (8. Sept.) steht freilich in alten Engl. Kalendern (Piper Kalendar. Agsa. 94; Bishop Bosworth psalter p. 104. 169), doch wird Himmelfahrt mehr ausgezeichnet. Q übersetzt richtig ‘August’, was auch Napier Lex. 92 belegt

15 Aug.; cf. Gl Maria 4. The Nativity of Mary (8 Sept.) does indeed appear in old English calendars (Piper Kalendar. Agsa. 94; Bishop Bosworth psalter p. 104. 169), but the Assumption is more highly distinguished. Q correctly translates ‘August’, which Napier Lex. 92 also attests
Q interpungiert richtig. Erst vor þeowum interpungieren H, Price; aber dann fehlt zu syn ein pluralisches Subjekt. Umgekehrt zählt auch schon 1. Nov. zu den Feiertagen der Unfreien B
Q punctuates correctly. H and Price punctuate only before þeowum; but then syn lacks a plural subject. Conversely, B even counts 1 Nov. among the holidays of the unfree
To make almsgiving possible, for the Church
nicht ‘to those to whom it may be most desirable to give’ (z. T. aus Q), wo ‘ihnen’ fehlt. Q scheint zu verstehen: ‘um ihre Arbeitszeit einem beliebigen oder einem früheren Wohltäter zu widmen’

not ‘to those to whom it may be most desirable to give’ (partly from Q), where ‘them’ is missing. Q seems to understand: ‘to devote their working time to any benefactor they please, or to a former one’

Der Besitz des Unfreien (s. Gl 22d—h; Fasten 8a) entsteht nur aus Almosen oder Arbeitsertrag in seinen Freistunden, die ihm der Herr liess. In Norwegen gibt ein Häuptling Acker zum Bebauen in Freistunden an Sklaven, die sich aus so Erspartem freikaufen sollen; Maurer Kr. Übschau I 414. ‘Arbeitszeit’ hwil galt als Wert; auch fronende Bauern müssen für jede Hufe dem Herrn drei Äcker pflügen ‘in ihrer eigenen hwile’; Urk. a. 901 Bi 594

The property of the unfree man (see Gl 22d—h; Fasten 8a) arises only from alms or from the earnings of his work in the free hours his lord left him. In Norway a chieftain gives slaves land to cultivate in their free hours, so that they may buy their freedom with what they save in this way; Maurer Kr. Übschau I 414. ‘Working time’ hwil counted as something of value; tenant peasants doing labour-service, too, must plough three acres for the lord for each hide ‘in their own hwile’; charter a. 901 Bi 594
‘freien’, statt des hiora ‘ihren, ihnen gehörigen’, Schmid. Zum adjektivischen ænig verbunden mit Possessiv im Sinne eines Indefinitums mit partitivem Genetiv vgl. Einenkel in Anglia 26, 559
‘free’, instead of hiora ‘their, belonging to them’, Schmid. On adjectival ænig combined with a possessive in the sense of an indefinite with partitive genitive, cf. Einenkel in Anglia 26, 559
nicht ‘Zeiten’, sondern ‘kurzen Zeitbruchstücken’. Q übersetzt hwil durch vicis, wohl verführt durch dessen afz. Entsprechung feiz, fieðe (s. Wb), die ‘Zeitpunkt’ bedeuten kann
not ‘times’ but ‘short fragments of time’. Q translates hwil by vicis, probably misled by its Old French equivalent feiz, fieðe (see Wb), which can mean ‘point in time’

note.seg: Liebermann, in his notes (iii. p. 60), translates esnewyrhtan as ‘knechtischen Arbeitern’; see also note to Abt. cap. 85, above. ‘Free men,’ Liebermann explains, includes ‘Hintersassen im Herrschaftsgut, Bauern und Kötter, die Fron leisten,’ and ‘Landarbeiter ohne Grundbesitz, die im Gutshofe, auch des Bauern, wohnen.’
15th August (Liebermann). Quadr. reads et in Augusto plena ebdomada ante festum beate Marie.

Ember days were days of fasting appointed by the Church to be observed in the four seasons of the year. Each fast occupied three days which, since the Council of Placentia a.d. 1095, have been the Wednesday, Friday and Saturday next following (1) The first Sunday in Lent, (2) Whitsunday, (3) Holy Cross Day (14th Sept.), (4) St Lucia’s Day (13th Dec.) (see N.E.D.).

The words þam þe him...for Godes noman are taken differently by Schmid, Liebermann, and previous editors, who place a comma after forgifen and interpret þam as dative singular, and þe as nominative to sie. The translation would then be ‘in order to give to him who is dearest to them etc.’ I take þe him to be dative plural of the relative.
